title: The Holland record and why she digs back for old songs
summary: She did 'Something to Remember You By' in Holland; she avoids currently popular songs, and the overlap between jazz and pop has gone.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well I don't know. I noticed on the last record that I heard, it's not chronologically the last. That's the one you made in Holland.
Yeah.
With Ted Easton's jazz band. You sang Something To Remember You By.
Right.
You know, it's something you've never done before.
Right. Well I --
You keep on doing new things.
'Something To Remember You By' is not new. It's an old song. It's a very old song.
That's what I say, I have to keep digging

back all the time, because I don't really like to do currently popular material.
In fact, if I do a song that's, say, less than five years old, it is a song that has come out -- so far as I'm concerned -- proven itself to sort of hit what I would say standard material.
Sure. That's been the big change in the music world, I guess, since the absence of rock and roll.
And that is, when you started your career, the songs that a jazz singer would sing and the popular songs of today, were very much overlapped.
That's right.
There is since the 1950's, the songs that sell in the millions are the records that're the best sellers.
It's absolutely not what you'd expect a jazz person to be doing.
Right.
Or, even a tasteful supper club vocalist.

So, you have to go back. Fortunately, there's a -- I won't say a vast repertoire but those are quite large.

Oh yes. You see, another problem that singers would have -- and I think singers like to feel that they're first, you know. So, if I dig up some old material, I can be the first who does that song today. And I have noticed lately, that a lot of things that I've been doing lately that I've been including in my repertoire, you're begining to hear them on albums made by other people. So, I think I'm discovering a lot of things for a lot of other people. But it doesn't make me mad, you know.
That's healthy influence.
Sure.
